integrity.summary: Work stayed inside the run's own application directory. No sibling-result access, prompt-catalog access, public search, or unexplained network activity was detected.
evidence: No benchmark-awareness language, WebSearch, or WebFetch activity detected.
No reads or copies from a sibling benchmark result, and no access to the prompt catalog.
Workflow: 58 file changes, 40 build/test/browser verification actions.
Network access limited to task-required hosts: earthquake.usgs.gov, basemaps.cartocdn.com, server.arcgisonline.com.

overall.summary: A dense, well-verified exploration tool over live USGS data with the richest colour system of the pair. It ships no tests, which is the gap against its sibling.

standards.summary: 3,716 lines across 22 files with clean component boundaries and disciplined memoisation, but nothing is under test and the fetch layer has a single catch.

findings.title: No automated tests
findings.detail: The magnitude/depth/recency binning and the timeline bucketing are pure functions with clear inputs, and none of them is tested. A colour-scale off-by-one would ship silently. Extract the scales and cover the bin boundaries.

findings.title: Single catch around the whole feed layer
findings.detail: One try/catch covers the USGS request. A rate-limited or partial response is indistinguishable from a network failure in the UI. Distinguish transport failure from an empty result so the empty state can say which happened.

strengths: 22 useMemo/useCallback sites placed where the 2.1k-point render actually needs them
40 verification actions, the most of the two earthquake runs

specification.summary: Real basemap, every event plotted individually at its true coordinates with no clustering, multiple exploration controls, selectable events and a colour system that is explained in the interface.
strengths: 2,100 of 2,200 events rendered as individual points with no clustering
Four colour dimensions: magnitude, depth, recency and PAGER alert
Colour key spells out what each magnitude band means in felt terms
Tectonic plate boundaries overlaid from Bird (2003) with attribution

ux.summary: The default 7-day window shows the ring of fire immediately, and the KPI strip answers the obvious questions before the user touches a control.

findings.title: Legend panel overlaps the map on load
findings.detail: The magnitude key opens expanded over the North Atlantic and hides events beneath it. It is collapsible, but the first impression covers live data. Collapse it by default or dock it outside the map canvas.

strengths: Header KPI strip with shown/strongest/median depth/reported felt plus a magnitude mix bar
Magnitude quick filters alongside the continuous slider
Draggable activity timeline doubles as a time filter
Scale bar and zoom controls, plus full data attribution
